PDPA2012.name: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 26 of 2012), 2020 Revised Edition
PDPA2012.status: In force. Current consolidated text as at 3 Sep 2026, incorporating Act 19 of 2025.

key_provisions.s 2(1): Definitions. 'employee' INCLUDES a volunteer; 'employment' INCLUDES working under an unpaid volunteer work relationship. Also defines 'evaluative purpose' (suitability/eligibility for employment, promotion, continuance, removal).
key_provisions.s 11(3)-(5): Must designate one or more individuals responsible for compliance (DPO), and must make the business contact information of at least one publicly available.
key_provisions.s 12: Accountability Obligation — develop and implement written policies and practices, develop a complaints process, communicate policies to staff, make information available on request.
key_provisions.ss 13-17: Consent Obligation, including s 15/15A deemed consent, s 16 withdrawal of consent, s 17 collection/use/disclosure without consent by reference to the First and Second Schedules.
key_provisions.s 20(4)-(5): Notification duty when relying on the employment-management exception: must inform the individual of the purpose on or before collection/use/disclosure, and on request provide business contact information of someone who can answer questions.
key_provisions.s 25: Retention Limitation Obligation — cease retention once the purpose is no longer served AND retention is no longer necessary for legal or business purposes. No fixed period.
key_provisions.s 26: Transfer Limitation Obligation — no transfer outside Singapore except per prescribed requirements ensuring comparable protection.
key_provisions.Part 6A, ss 26A-26E: Mandatory data breach notification. Inserted by Act 40 of 2020. In force 1 Feb 2021.
key_provisions.Part 6B, ss 26F-26J + Twelfth Schedule: Data portability. Enacted by Act 40 of 2020 but NOT COMMENCED — absent from the current consolidated Act's table of contents as at 5 Sep 2026.
key_provisions.s 48J(3): Financial penalty cap: 10% of annual turnover in Singapore where that turnover exceeds $10 million; otherwise $1 million.
key_provisions.Part 9B, ss 48C-48F: Offences affecting personal data by individuals — s 48D unauthorised disclosure, s 48E improper use, s 48F unauthorised re-identification. Fine up to $5,000 and/or up to 2 years' imprisonment.
key_provisions.First Schedule Part 3 para 1: Legitimate Interests exception. Requires a WRITTEN assessment BEFORE collection/use/disclosure, and reasonable access for the individual to information about it.
key_provisions.First Schedule Part 3 para 10: Employment-management exception — reasonable for entering into an employment relationship, or managing or terminating it.
key_provisions.First Schedule Part 5 / Second Schedule: Business improvement purposes. Inter-group version requires a contract, other agreement or binding corporate rules requiring appropriate safeguards.

PDPA-AMD-2020.name: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2020 (Act 40 of 2020)
PDPA-AMD-2020.status: Passed 2 Nov 2020, assented 25 Nov 2020, gazetted 10 Dec 2020. Bulk in force 1 Feb 2021. Section 24 (turnover-based penalty) in force 1 Oct 2022. Part 6B data portability still not commenced.

PDPA-BREACH-REGS-2021.name: Personal Data Protection (Notification of Data Breaches) Regulations 2021 (S 64/2021)
PDPA-BREACH-REGS-2021.status: In force 1 Feb 2021 (reg 1). Informal consolidation to 15 Oct 2024.

key_provisions.reg 3: 'Significant harm' deemed where the breach involves the individual's full name/alias/identification number PLUS personal data listed in the Schedule — including wages/income, credit/charge/debit card numbers, bank account numbers, net worth, investments; and specified sensitive categories.
key_provisions.reg 4: 'Significant scale' — the prescribed number of affected individuals is 500.
key_provisions.s 26D(1) timeline: Notify PDPC as soon as practicable, but in any case no later than 3 CALENDAR DAYS after the day the organisation makes its assessment.
key_provisions.s 26C: Duty to conduct an assessment once the organisation has credible grounds to believe a data breach has occurred. This is what starts the 3-day clock.

key_provisions.reg 10: Transferring organisation must take appropriate steps to ensure the overseas recipient is bound by legally enforceable obligations giving comparable protection.
key_provisions.reg 11: 'Legally enforceable obligations' = law, contract (must require a comparable protection standard AND specify the destination countries), binding corporate rules (related corporations only, with specified content), or another legally binding instrument.
key_provisions.reg 12: Alternative route — recipient holding a specified certification is deemed to satisfy the comparable-protection requirement.
key_provisions.reg 15: Prescribes the content of the written assessment required for the Legitimate Interests exception; reg 15(3) requires the organisation to RETAIN a copy of the assessment throughout the period it relies on the exception.

PDPA-AMD-REGS-2026.name: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S 86/2026)
PDPA-AMD-REGS-2026.status: IN FORCE 2 MARCH 2026. Made 26 Feb 2026. THE MOST RECENT SUBSTANTIVE PDPA-SIDE CHANGE — six months old at the date of this corpus.
PDPA-AMD-REGS-2026.effect: Expanded the certifications recognised under reg 12 for cross-border transfer beyond APEC CBPR/PRP to include the Global CBPR System and the Global Privacy Recognition for Processors System.

PDPC-AG-SELECTED-TOPICS.name: PDPC Advisory Guidelines on the PDPA for Selected Topics, Chapter 6 (Employment)

key_paragraphs.6.19: Employment-relationship collection/use/disclosure 'would not require the consent' of employees under the management exception — but NOTIFICATION of purposes is still required.
key_paragraphs.6.20: PDPC does not prescribe the form or manner of notification; employment contract, handbook or intranet notice all suffice. A general upfront notification of purposes is enough.
key_paragraphs.6.21: Non-exhaustive list of management purposes: pre-employment health screening, reference checks, payroll, IT resource monitoring, work scheduling, disciplinary checks, staff-directory photos, benefits administration, audits, WSH, performance management.
key_paragraphs.6.22-6.23: Consent IS still required for purposes unrelated to the employment relationship.
key_paragraphs.6.24-6.25: Distinguishes the evaluative-purpose exception (no notification needed) from the employment-management exception (notification needed).
key_paragraphs.6.27-6.28: Retention — may keep former-employee data for a valid ongoing business purpose, but not indefinitely without a defined purpose.
key_paragraphs.6.1-6.13: Job applicants are expressly within scope, generally via ordinary consent/deemed consent rather than the employment-management exception (per 6.32, that exception applies once there is or will be an actual employment relationship).
key_paragraphs.interns: The word 'intern' or 'internship' does NOT appear anywhere in the 62-page guidelines. PDPC has issued no guidance specifically addressing interns.

EA1968.name: Employment Act 1968
EA1968.status: In force. s 26 amended by Act 19 of 2025 with effect from 5 Dec 2025 (new permitted deductions for MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums).

key_provisions.s 2(1): 'employee' = a person who has entered into or works under a contract of service. 'Contract of service' includes an apprenticeship contract or agreement. Excludes seafarers and domestic workers.
key_provisions.s 10(3): Minimum notice absent contractual provision: 1 day if < 26 weeks; 1 week if 26 weeks to < 2 years; 2 weeks if 2 to < 5 years; 4 weeks if >= 5 years.
key_provisions.s 11: Either party may terminate without notice by paying salary in lieu.
key_provisions.s 21: Salary payable within 7 days after the end of the salary period; overtime pay within 14 days after the end of the salary period in which it was worked.
key_provisions.ss 26-32: Deductions. s 26 no deductions unless authorised. s 27(1)(a)-(k) permitted categories. s 29 damage/loss deduction capped at one quarter of one month's wages. s 30(2) accommodation/amenity deductions capped at one quarter. s 32(1) TOTAL deductions in any salary period capped at 50%, excluding s 27(1)(a), (f) and (j).
key_provisions.s 35: Part 4 applies to workmen earning <= $4,500/month and other employees (non-managerial, non-executive) earning <= $2,600/month, in each case excluding overtime, bonus, AWS, productivity incentive and allowances.
key_provisions.s 36(1): One whole rest day per week (unpaid), normally Sunday or as the employer determines.
key_provisions.s 37: Pay for work on a rest day.
key_provisions.s 38: Normal hours max 8/day or 44/week (variations to 9/day, 44-48/week under provisos); s 38(4) overtime at not less than 1.5x hourly basic rate; s 38(5) overtime capped at 72 hours a month; s 38(8) 12-hour daily cap except in listed emergencies.
key_provisions.s 88A: Annual leave — entitlement after 3 months' service; 7 days for the first 12 months, +1 day per subsequent 12 months, capped at 14 days; proration for partial years.
key_provisions.s 89: Sick leave — >= 3 but < 6 months' service gives prorated entitlement (5/8/11 days outpatient scaling with months served); >= 6 months gives full entitlement of 14 days outpatient, or if hospitalised the lesser of 60 days or (14 days + days hospitalised).
key_provisions.s 95A: Key Employment Terms in writing within 14 days of the start of employment, for employees who started on or after 1 Apr 2016 and are employed for the prescribed minimum period.
key_provisions.s 96: Itemised pay slips for every employee.

EA-KET-REGS-2016.name: Employment (Employment Records, Key Employment Terms and Pay Slips) Regulations 2016

key_provisions.reg 6(1): The prescribed minimum period of service for the s 95A KET duty is a continuous period of 14 DAYS. An intern engaged for 14 days or more under a contract of service must be given written KETs.
key_provisions.regs 7-8: Pay slip timing (on or near the salary payment date) and form.

MOM-INTERN-COVERAGE.name: MOM FAQ — intern coverage under the Employment Act and WICA
MOM-INTERN-COVERAGE.quote: The EA and WICA cover employees engaged under a contract of service. Students undergoing internships are covered if there is a contract of service that establishes an employer-employee relationship between the employer and the intern.
MOM-INTERN-COVERAGE.test: Contract of service vs contract for service decided on control, ownership of factors of production, and economic considerations. No single conclusive test; factors considered holistically.

WICA2019.name: Work Injury Compensation Act 2019
WICA2019.status: In force. Amended by Act 30 of 2024 (Part 3A, platform operators/workers) with provisions from 15 Oct 2024 and 1 Jan 2025.

key_provisions.s 3(1): 'employee' = an individual who has entered into or works under a contract of service, subject to Third Schedule exclusions.
key_provisions.s 24: Employer must be insured against liabilities under the Act.
key_provisions.s 25: Failure to insure is an offence — fine up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months.

WICA2019.mom_scope: Insurance mandatory for all employees doing manual work regardless of salary, and all employees doing non-manual work earning <= $2,600/month. On a contract of service, virtually every intern in this corpus falls under the $2,600 threshold.

CPF.name: Central Provident Fund — contributions for interns and students
CPF.quote: CPF contributions are payable for all local employees, including interns, when there is an employer-employee relationship, i.e. a contract of service.
CPF.exemption: Employers may be exempt for interns who are students enrolled in MOE-subsidised institutions and employed for training approved by their educational institution, with supporting documentation retained. If the internship is not endorsed by the educational institution, CPF contributions remain payable.
CPF.rate_changes: From 1 Jan 2027, senior-worker rates rise: above 55-60 from 34% to 35.5% total; above 60-65 from 25% to 26% total. Source: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/infohub/news/cpf-related-announcements/new-contribution-rates

WFA2025.name: Workplace Fairness Act 2025 (Act 8 of 2025)
WFA2025.status: NOT IN FORCE. Passed by Parliament 8 Jan 2025, assented 3 Feb 2025, gazetted 14 Feb 2025. SSO shows 'Uncommenced' as at 5 Sep 2026. s 1 provides commencement on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notification. MOM's stated target is end-2027.

key_provisions.s 2: 'employee' = an individual who has entered into or works under a contract of service with an employer. 'Contract of service' takes the meaning in s 2(1) of the Employment Act 1968.
key_provisions.s 4(1)(a) and 4(2): Act does not apply (except for s 26) to an employer employing fewer than the prescribed number of individuals. Prescribed number is 25, substitutable by the Minister by Gazette notification.
key_provisions.s 8: Protected characteristics: (a) age; (b) nationality; (c) sex; (d) marital status; (e) pregnancy; (f) caregiving responsibilities; (g) race; (h) religion; (i) language ability; (j) disability; (k) mental health condition. ss 9-16 define each.
key_provisions.s 19: Discrimination by advertisement or description — unlawful to publish in Singapore an advertisement or description relating to possible employment that mentions, expressly or by implication, a protected characteristic as a condition, criterion, requirement, advantage, disadvantage or disqualification.
key_provisions.s 26: Fair consideration — applies to ALL employers regardless of size. Before applying for certain work passes, must have published a compliant job advertisement, considered all responses in good faith and fairly, and the foreign hire's job and salary must match what was advertised.
key_provisions.s 27: Employer MUST develop a written grievance-handling process covering inquiry, review, informing the employee of the outcome, keeping written records for a stated period, and non-disclosure. s 27(2): must inform all employees in writing of the process.
key_provisions.s 28: Prohibits retaliation against employees who raise grievances or participate in proceedings.

WFDRA2025.name: Workplace Fairness (Dispute Resolution) Act 2025 (Act 22 of 2025)
WFDRA2025.status: NOT IN FORCE. Passed 4 Nov 2025, assented 25 Nov 2025. SSO shows 'Uncommenced' as at 5 Sep 2026.
WFDRA2025.effect: Adds mediation of workplace fairness disputes and a statutory tort of discrimination; new ss 36B-36C confer Employment Claims Tribunal jurisdiction via s 12A of the Employment Claims Act 2016, excluding claims above the tribunal limit. MOM states the ECT will hear discrimination claims up to $250,000, with mediation required first.

TGFEP.name: Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) / TAFEP
TGFEP.status: In force as soft law. Will run ALONGSIDE the WFA, not be superseded by it. Employers under 25 employees remain bound by TGFEP even though exempt from most of the WFA.

TG-FWAR.name: Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests
TG-FWAR.status: In effect from 1 DECEMBER 2024, replacing the 2014 Advisory and the 2017 Tripartite Standard on FWAs.
TG-FWAR.verified: Existence and 1 Dec 2024 effective date verified. The detailed procedural requirements (response deadline in working days, reasons for rejection, service qualifying period) are UNVERIFIED — see unverified_claims.

RRA1993.name: Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993
RRA1993.status: In force. Minimum retirement age rose to 64 years from 1 July 2026 for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
RRA1993.verified: Retirement age 64 from 1 Jul 2026 verified. The re-employment age ceiling figure is UNVERIFIED.

PWA2024.name: Platform Workers Act 2024
PWA2024.relevance: Not engaged by this corpus — no platform work. Recorded as checked-and-not-engaged.

coverage_analysis.headline: Coverage is NOT uniform across instruments, and the asymmetry is the most legally interesting thing in this corpus.

findings.coverage: BROADEST. s 2(1) defines 'employee' to INCLUDE a volunteer, and 'employment' to INCLUDE working under an unpaid volunteer work relationship. So PDPA coverage does not depend on a contract of service at all.
findings.intern_position: An intern — paid or unpaid — is very likely within the extended 'employment' definition and therefore within the employment-management exception and the s 20(4) notification duty. But PDPC has issued NO guidance specifically on interns: the word does not appear anywhere in the 62-page Selected Topics guidelines. This is an inference from statutory text, not a settled PDPC position. Flag it, do not assert it.
findings.confidence: medium-high on the statutory definition (verified); medium on application to interns (inference)

findings.coverage: NARROWER. Turns entirely on whether there is a contract of service. MOM: 'Students undergoing internships are covered if there is a contract of service that establishes an employer-employee relationship.'
findings.intern_position: DOC-001, DOC-002, DOC-003 and DOC-004 all pay an allowance, direct the work, set hours and require exclusivity — strong control indicators. Each is likely a contract of service, but this is a factual determination, not a label the employer can choose. DOC-003 cl 2.3 expressly disclaims employee benefits; that disclaimer does not decide the statutory question.
findings.part_4_position: Even where the EA applies, Part 4 (hours, overtime, rest days) applies only to non-workmen earning <= $2,600/month (s 35). Every allowance in this corpus is below that, so Part 4 DOES bite — which makes the overtime and rest-day clauses live rather than decorative.
findings.confidence: high on the statutory test; medium on the outcome for any given document

findings.coverage: NARROWEST, twice over. First, it is not in force at all. Second, when it commences, s 4(1)(a) exempts employers with fewer than 25 employees from everything except s 26.
findings.intern_position: s 2 borrows 'contract of service' from the Employment Act, so the same test applies. The Act does not mention interns or trainees anywhere — neither included nor excluded. A genuinely unresolved gap.
findings.corpus_effect: DOC-001 and DOC-002 (multinationals) would be covered on commencement. DOC-003 and DOC-004 (small law firms) would very likely fall under the 25-employee exemption and be bound only by s 26 plus the TGFEP. Same regulatory change, opposite operational consequence.

findings.coverage: Contract-of-service test again (s 3(1)). MOM: covers any local or foreign employee under a contract of service or apprenticeship, regardless of salary, age or citizenship.
findings.intern_position: Insurance is mandatory for non-manual employees earning <= $2,600/month. Every intern in this corpus is below that. So an intern on a contract of service MUST be covered by WIC insurance, and failure to insure is an offence under s 25.
findings.corpus_effect: Only DOC-001 mentions work injury compensation insurance at all, and only conditionally ('where required under applicable laws'). DOC-002, DOC-003 and DOC-004 are silent. DOC-003 cl 2.3 affirmatively says the intern gets no health insurance.

findings.coverage: Contract-of-service test, with a student-specific carve-out.
findings.intern_position: CPF is payable for interns where there is an employer-employee relationship, EXCEPT where the intern is a student at an MOE-subsidised institution AND the training is approved by the institution AND the employer holds supporting documentation. If the internship is not endorsed by the institution, CPF remains payable.
findings.corpus_effect: This is a documentary condition, not an automatic exemption. Only DOC-001 addresses CPF at all, and it does so on a citizenship/PR condition without referencing the student-endorsement route. No document in the corpus records whether institutional endorsement was obtained.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: Your internship with the Employer will commence on [START DATE] and end on [END DATE]. You are required to carry out such duties as are consistent with your position and as may from time to time be assigned to you in the Employer's sole and absolute discretion, including but not limited to drafting correspondence and legal documents/ conducting legal research on various matters. The whole of your working time, attention and abilities will be devoted to the business and affairs of the Employer and/or the EssilorLuxottica Group. As long as you are an intern of the Employer, you shall not enter into or hold any other employment or engagement, whether paid or unpaid, without obtaining the prior written consent of the Employer. You shall report to the [SUPERVISOR ROLE: Legal Counsel].

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The degree of control this clause asserts — duties at the employer's sole discretion, whole of working time, exclusivity — is precisely the evidence MOM's control test looks for. This clause is what makes the engagement a contract of service and therefore pulls the whole document into the Employment Act.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_heading: TERM OF SERVICE — work pass condition
clauses.clause_text: Your internship shall be subject to and conditional upon: (a) where applicable, you obtaining, possessing and/or maintaining at all times during the period of your internship a valid work pass to work in Singapore and any other requirements pursuant to applicable laws;

regulatory_dependencies.provision: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act 1990; Training Employment Pass / Training Work Permit / Work Holiday Pass
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Conditions the engagement on a valid work pass. Drafted generically ('where applicable', 'any other requirements pursuant to applicable laws'), which is the resilient drafting pattern — it survives changes to pass types and salary thresholds without amendment.

On commencement, s 26 will bind ALL employers regardless of size before applying for certain work passes — compliant job advertisement, good-faith consideration of responses, and the hire's job and salary matching what was advertised. This clause currently addresses only the candidate's obligation to hold a pass; it says nothing about the employer's own pre-application advertising duty.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_heading: TERM OF SERVICE — background checks and verification
clauses.clause_text: (b) where the Employer deems necessary, you satisfying any background checks required by the Employer; and (c) the satisfactory verification of all information provided by you to the Employer.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: First Schedule Part 3 para 2 (evaluative purposes); s 2(1) definition of 'evaluative purpose'
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Background checks and verification of candidate-supplied information are the paradigm case of an evaluative purpose — determining suitability or eligibility for employment. PDPC's guidelines give 'obtaining a reference from a prospective employee's former employer' as a worked example.

The evaluative-purpose exception does NOT carry a notification duty, whereas the employment-management exception does. This clause therefore sits on a different legal basis from clause 14, even though both concern the same person's data — a distinction the document does not draw.

pdpa_impact.explanation: Not wrong, but drafted as though consent were the operative basis. Since the 2020 amendments restructured the First Schedule, background checks of this kind rest on the evaluative-purposes exception, which requires no consent and no notification. The clause is doing no legal work it needs to do.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: Your internship allowance shall be [BANDED: SGD 1,000-2,000] for each full calendar month of work. Such allowance will be paid on or about the 28th of each calendar month (i.e. in arrears) unless otherwise advised by the Employer, by direct transfer into the designated bank account in Singapore titled in your name.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 21 (salary within 7 days of the end of the salary period)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: 'On or about the 28th' is a soft formulation. s 21 requires payment within 7 days after the end of the salary period. If the salary period is the calendar month, paying on the 28th pays before period end, which is compliant; but 'or about' and 'unless otherwise advised by the Employer' leave room for a payment date that would breach s 21.
The allowance is below the $2,600 non-workman threshold, so Part 4 applies if the engagement is a contract of service.

NON-OBVIOUS DEPENDENCY. The Schedule to reg 3 lists wages/income and bank account numbers among the data types that, combined with a full name or identification number, make a breach one of 'significant harm' and therefore notifiable. This clause causes the employer to hold exactly that combination for the intern. The salary clause is a data-breach-severity dependency, not just a payment clause.

pdpa_impact.explanation: The clause creates a personal-data holding (name + bank account + income) that reg 3 deems capable of significant harm. Nothing in this document, or any document in the corpus, tells anyone what to do if that holding is compromised. See scenario PDPA-S1.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: The Employer shall reimburse you for all reasonable expenses properly incurred by you in the performance of your duties, subject to (i) the Employer's prevailing policies and procedures on the reimbursement of expenses, and (ii) you providing the Employer with all relevant receipts. All amounts payable by the Employer to you shall be subject to any deduction and/or withholding which the Employer may be entitled or required to make under applicable laws. You expressly agree that the following deductions may be made by the Employer from your allowance: (i) deductions for absence from work; (ii) deductions for damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to you for custody or for loss of money for which you are required to account, where the damage or loss is directly attributable to your neglect or default; (iii) deductions for the adjustment of any overpayment of allowance; (iv) deductions made with your written consent; and (v) any other statutorily prescribed deductions.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The five listed categories track s 27(1) closely — this clause was clearly drafted against the Employment Act. Category (ii) tracks s 27(1)(b).

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 29 (damage/loss capped at one quarter of one month's wages) and s 32(1) (total deductions capped at 50% of the salary period)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The clause reproduces the permitted CATEGORIES but omits both statutory CAPS. A clause that says damage deductions may be made without saying they are capped at a quarter of a month's wages is incomplete on its face.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 26 as amended by Act 19 of 2025 with effect from 5 Dec 2025
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: STALE. The permitted-deduction list was extended on 5 Dec 2025 to add categories where the employer acts as agent for recovery of MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums (s 26(1)(d)-(e)). This document is dated 16 Apr 2026 — four months AFTER the amendment — and its enumerated list does not reflect it. The catch-all '(v) any other statutorily prescribed deductions' saves it legally, but the enumeration is out of date.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: Either the Employer or you may terminate your internship at any time by giving two weeks' written notice of termination to the other party, provided always that either party may, by written notice to the other party, terminate your internship immediately or with such shorter period of notice than that set out above. In such a case, the party giving such notice shall pay to the other party a sum equal to your gross monthly allowance in respect of the period or balance of the period of notice that is otherwise required to be given. Notwithstanding anything contained herein, the Employer may terminate your internship immediately by giving you written notice of termination and without any compensation whatsoever if: you are absent from work for more than two (2) working days continuously without prior leave, without reasonable excuse or without informing or attempting to inform the Employer of the excuse for your absence; you are found to have committed any material breach or non-observance of any of the terms of this letter; you are found to have engaged in any conduct tending to bring into disrepute or affecting the business of the Employer; you are convicted of any criminal offence; or you are found to have engaged in any act of misconduct or willful neglect in the discharge of your duties hereunder. Apart from terminations due to misconduct or your own voluntary resignation, you shall be paid in lieu of any unused and accrued leave (pro-rated where applicable). Upon the termination of your internship for any reason whatsoever, you shall immediately return to the Employer all property or assets belonging to or provided by the Employer, including computers, keys, documents, Confidential Information, files, records, correspondence, client, customer, supplier or other lists, equipment or any other items of any kind which may have been prepared by you or come into your possession, custody or control during the course of or as a result of your internship.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Two weeks' notice EXCEEDS the statutory minimum of 1 day for service under 26 weeks, so the clause is compliant and more generous. Note the direction: this clause is resilient to a tightening of s 10(3) up to the two-week mark.
The payment-in-lieu mechanic mirrors s 11.

The return-of-property limb runs one way only: the intern returns the employer's data. Nothing addresses the employer's own duty to cease retaining the intern's personal data once the purpose is spent. s 25 is an obligation on the ORGANISATION, and this clause is silent on it.

On commencement, the broad 'material breach or non-observance' and 'conduct tending to bring into disrepute' summary-termination grounds will need to be read subject to the prohibition on retaliating against an employee who has raised a grievance or participated in proceedings.

pdpa_impact.explanation: Says something true and useful (return the employer's data) but omits the reciprocal s 25 duty entirely. An asymmetric return-of-property clause is the single most common PDPA gap in employment templates.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: If you are or become a citizen or permanent resident of Singapore, the Employer shall make the prescribed contributions to the Central Provident Fund in accordance with applicable laws.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: CPF Board guidance on interns and students
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The clause conditions CPF on citizenship/PR status alone. CPF Board guidance adds a second axis the clause ignores: the student-endorsement exemption, available only where the intern is at an MOE-subsidised institution AND the training is approved by the institution AND the employer holds supporting documentation. The clause's 'in accordance with applicable laws' catch-all covers this legally, but operationally the document does not prompt anyone to obtain or retain the endorsement evidence.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: Your usual working hours shall be in accordance with the Employer's prevailing practices, which is currently [0900 hours to 1800 hours] from [Monday to Friday], with [one (1)] hour for lunch break. However, you acknowledge and agree that you may from time to time be required to work beyond the aforementioned hours in order to fulfill your duties and responsibilities to the Employer, depending on the business needs and exigences of the Employer. In such a case, you will be entitled to overtime pay based on statutory rates, if applicable. If you are entitled to overtime payment, this payment shall be made by the Employer to you within 14 days of the last day of the allowance period. Your rest day is every Sunday. You will be eligible to participate in the Employer's flexible working arrangements in accordance with the Employer's prevailing policy, which may be amended from time to time at the Employer's sole and absolute discretion.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 38 (hours and overtime), s 38(4) 1.5x rate, s 38(5) 72-hour monthly cap, s 38(8) 12-hour daily cap
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The clause defers to 'statutory rates, if applicable' rather than reciting 1.5x — a deliberately resilient drafting choice that survives a change to the multiplier without amendment. But it omits the 72-hour monthly and 12-hour daily caps entirely, so it correctly prices overtime while failing to limit it.
The 14-day overtime payment period tracks s 21 exactly.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 36(1) (one whole rest day per week)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: 'Your rest day is every Sunday' implements s 36(1) directly.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests, in effect 1 Dec 2024
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The FWA sentence is drafted as a discretionary employer benefit ('eligible to participate ... at the Employer's sole and absolute discretion'). The TG-FWAR, in effect since 1 Dec 2024, frame FWAs around a REQUEST process rather than pure employer discretion. This document (Apr 2026) post-dates the guidelines by 16 months and does not reflect them.
regulatory_dependencies.confidence: medium — existence and effective date verified; the specific procedural requirements are UNVERIFIED

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: Your leave entitlement will be 7 days per calendar year, such leave accruing on a pro-rata basis throughout such year and in accordance with the Employer's prevailing policy. During the first (3) three months of your internship, you will not be entitled to any paid leave. Thereafter, you shall be entitled to utilise your leave entitlement at such time or times as shall be agreed with the Employer. You shall obtain the Employer's written approval for you to utilise your leave by no later than the date falling 14 days prior to the date of the intended utilisation of your leave. Leave may only be taken at times that are convenient to the Employer.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: 7 days and the 3-month qualifying period both track s 88A exactly. This engagement runs 15 May to 18 Dec — over 7 months — so the qualifying period is met and the entitlement is live.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: You are entitled to paid sick leave of (a) 14 days per calendar year (if no hospitalisation is required) and (b) 60 days per calendar year (if hospitalisation is required) which is inclusive of the 14 days non-hospitalisation leave, prorated with the duration of your internship in accordance with applicable laws. You shall immediately, or as soon as reasonably practicable, notify the Employer by telephone if you become incapable of performing your duties under this letter due to sickness or injury. Upon your return to work, you shall furnish to the Employer a certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner covering your period of absence in respect of each claim for sick leave. Failure to do so will render your absence unauthorized and may result in the Employer withholding sick leave pay and/or taking disciplinary action against you. You shall also be provided with work injury compensation insurance where required under applicable laws.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: 14/60 days tracks s 89(1). But the clause states the FULL entitlement without the s 89 service-qualifying tiers: under 3 months' service there is no entitlement, and between 3 and 6 months it is prorated on a 5/8/11-day scale. 'Prorated with the duration of your internship in accordance with applicable laws' gestures at this without stating it.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 24 (must be insured), s 25 (offence not to be)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: 'Where required under applicable laws' is doing a lot of work. On a contract of service with an allowance under $2,600/month, WIC insurance is MANDATORY, and failure to insure is an offence carrying up to $10,000 and 12 months. The conditional phrasing makes a mandatory obligation read as contingent.

NON-OBVIOUS DEPENDENCY. The medical-certificate requirement makes the employer a holder of the intern's health data. The Schedule to reg 3 lists specified health categories which, combined with name or identification number, deem a breach to cause significant harm. A sick-leave clause is therefore also a breach-severity clause.

On commencement, 'mental health condition' becomes a protected characteristic, defined by reference to diagnosis by a registered medical practitioner. A clause that routes every medical certificate to the employer and attaches disciplinary consequences to non-production will interact directly with that protection.

pdpa_impact.explanation: The clause compels disclosure of health data to the employer but says nothing about how that data is handled, who sees it, or how long it is kept. Health data is in the reg 3 significant-harm Schedule.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: The nature of your internship with the Employer means that you will have access to or will become acquainted with confidential information which includes, without limitation: (a) all information that derives independent economic value, actual or potential, from not being generally known to, and not being readily ascertainable by proper means by, other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use; (b) all information made known to you as a consequence of your internship with the Employer; and (c) non-public information including, but not limited to, information relating to business affairs, trade secrets, turnover figures, service marks, products, financial accounts and reports, prospects research, financing, specifications, test results, research and development, any industrial property right or Intellectual Property Right that is not yet filed or published, data, methods, processes and procedures of operation, business or marketing or sales plans, strategies, licensed documentation, agreements, employees and employment policies and practices, customers, product costing and pricing, data surveys, client, supplier and customer lists, original samples, diagrams, records, and reports (collectively, "Confidential Information"). It is a condition of this letter, and you covenant and undertake to: (a) keep confidential all Confidential Information, and not disclose any Confidential Information to any person except: as required by law; or with the prior written consent of the Employer; or to the Employer's employees, interns, agents or advisors in the due performance of your duties (provided that such persons are also bound by a duty of confidentiality); (b) refrain from using any Confidential Information other than in connection with your internship; (d) maintain proper and secure custody of all Confidential Information and use your best endeavours to prevent the use or disclosure of the Confidential Information to or by third parties; (e) return, destroy or delete any or all Confidential Information promptly upon the termination of your internship with the Employer and at any time upon request of the Employer; and (f) keep your allowance and remuneration information strictly confidential.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: CENTRAL PDPA DEPENDENCY. The definition expressly captures 'employees and employment policies and practices' and 'client, supplier and customer lists' — i.e. third parties' personal data. Since 1 Feb 2021 the intern faces PERSONAL criminal liability under s 48D (unauthorised disclosure) and s 48E (improper use), carrying up to $5,000 and 2 years. The clause frames the entire risk as contractual, owed to the employer, enforceable by the employer. It never tells the intern that mishandling this data is a criminal offence against the individuals whose data it is.
The 'proper and secure custody' and 'best endeavours' obligations are the contractual expression of the employer's own s 24 duty, pushed onto the intern.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 26C (duty to assess) read with s 26D(1) (3 calendar days)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: CRITICAL OPERATIONAL GAP. The 3-calendar-day clock to notify PDPC runs from the employer's ASSESSMENT, and the s 26C duty to assess is triggered by the employer having credible grounds to believe a breach occurred. Credible grounds usually arrive because a member of staff escalates. This clause imposes confidentiality duties but creates NO internal reporting or escalation duty. An intern who spots a breach is contractually told to keep quiet, not to report — which structurally endangers the statutory deadline.

pdpa_impact.explanation: The clause is not contradicted by the PDPA — everything it says remains true. It is insufficient in two specific ways: it does not surface the intern's personal criminal exposure under ss 48D-48E, and it does not create the internal escalation duty that the employer's own 3-day notification clock depends on. This is the strongest single clause in the corpus for demonstrating 'insufficient' as distinct from 'contradicted'.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: You agree that all rights to all material created in the course of your internship with the Employer (including ownership of physical material) shall be deemed created or made in pursuance of the terms of this letter and in the course of your internship with the Employer, and shall accordingly vest in the Employer automatically. You hereby assign all Intellectual Property Rights to which you may now or at any time in the future be entitled to the Employer absolutely for as long as such rights subsist. To the extent that such Intellectual Property Rights do not vest automatically and/or are not assigned, you shall hold the same on trust for the Employer. You hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waive all moral rights to which you may now or at any time in the future be entitled to in respect of the material created and/or made by you in the course of your internship. You agree that this Clause shall be construed as a formal waiver for the purposes of Part 7 of the Copyright Act 2021.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: Part 7 (moral rights), as cited by the document itself
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The clause names its own dependency, which is unusually good drafting — it declares the instrument it relies on, so a change to that instrument is machine-detectable. UNVERIFIED: I did not fetch the Copyright Act 2021 to confirm that Part 7 is the moral rights Part. Do not assert the Part number to judges without checking.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: You hereby consent to the Employer collecting, using, processing, and/or disclosing any or all personal data (in manual, electronic or any other form) relevant to your internship, subject to a duty of confidentiality, for the purposes set out in the Group Employee Privacy Notice 2022 (as may be updated from time to time). You further accept and agree that your personal data may be transferred (in or outside Singapore) to third parties including but not limited to the Employer's Affiliates, the Employer's insurers, bankers, other regulatory bodies, governmental organizations, and to other companies engaged in contractual activities on the Employer's behalf, to be used for the purposes mentioned in the Employee Privacy Notice 2022. Where your personal data is transferred out of Singapore, the Employer will take reasonable steps to ensure that your personal data continues to receive a standard of protection that is at least comparable to that provided under applicable Singapore law. You may direct any queries on personal data matters to the Employer's data protection officer, who may be contacted at [REDACTED — DPO EMAIL] or such other contact as the Employer may notify you.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: THE ANCHOR CLAUSE FOR THE DEMO. Drafted as a consent clause. Consent is withdrawable under s 16. So the document's entire stated legal basis for handling the intern's data can be unilaterally revoked by the intern at any time.

The employer did not need this consent. Since the 2020 amendments restructured the First Schedule, collection, use and disclosure reasonable for entering into, managing or terminating an employment relationship is exempt from consent altogether. Relying on consent instead of the exception is choosing a weaker, revocable basis over a stronger, non-revocable one.

What the employer DOES owe under the exception is notification of purposes, and on request the business contact information of someone who can answer questions. The clause delegates purposes wholesale to an external 'Group Employee Privacy Notice 2022 (as may be updated from time to time)' — a document not attached, not reproduced, and expressly mutable without the intern's agreement.

PDPC states expressly that employment-relationship handling 'would not require the consent' of employees, and that a general upfront notification of purposes suffices — an employment contract is an accepted vehicle for that notification. The guidelines were revised 23 May 2024; this document is dated 16 Apr 2026 and still uses the pre-2020 consent architecture.
The clause promises 'reasonable steps to ensure ... a standard of protection that is at least comparable'. That is the language of s 26 itself, not of the implementing regulation.

reg 11 requires 'legally enforceable obligations' — law, a CONTRACT specifying the destination countries and requiring a comparable standard, BINDING CORPORATE RULES for related-corporation transfers with prescribed content, or another legally binding instrument. 'Reasonable steps' is not one of the four routes. The clause also names no destination countries, which reg 11 requires of the contract route.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: reg 12 as amended, in force 2 March 2026
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: THE LIVE CHANGE. Six months before this corpus was assembled, the recognised certification route was expanded beyond APEC CBPR/PRP to include the Global CBPR System and the Global Privacy Recognition for Processors System. This document was signed on 16 Apr 2026 — six weeks AFTER the change — and does not reference any certification route.

The clause names a DPO contact. This is the only document in the corpus that does. s 11(5) additionally requires the business contact information to be made available to the PUBLIC, not merely to the intern — putting it in a private contract does not by itself discharge that.
Silent. No reference to breach notification anywhere in the clause or the document, five and a half years after Part 6A came into force.
DORMANT DEPENDENCY. Enacted in 2020, still not in force. If commenced, a clause built on consent-plus-external-privacy-notice would need a portability request pathway it currently has nowhere to put.

pdpa_impact.explanation: Three distinct failures in one clause, which is what makes it the demo's anchor. (1) INSUFFICIENT on cross-border transfer: 'reasonable steps' is not one of reg 11's four routes to legally enforceable obligations, and no destination countries are specified. (2) STALE on legal basis: built on consent when the First Schedule Part 3 para 10 exception has been available since 2021, and PDPC's May 2024 guidelines say consent is not required — the employer has chosen a revocable basis over a non-revocable one. (3) NEWLY REQUIRED: no breach-notification pathway despite Part 6A being in force since 1 Feb 2021, and no reference to the certification route expanded on 2 March 2026.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter (Legal Intern), electronically signed
clauses.clause_text: The terms and conditions of this letter are to be construed in accordance with the laws of the Republic of Singapore. Each party irrevocably agrees to submit all disputes and/or claims in relation to, arising out of, or in connection with this letter to the courts of the Republic of Singapore, which shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to resolve any such disputes and/or claims.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: new ss 36B-36C, via s 12A Employment Claims Act 2016 — NOT IN FORCE
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The clause routes ALL disputes to the courts. On commencement of the WFDRA, discrimination claims up to $250,000 would go to the Employment Claims Tribunal after compulsory mediation, not to the courts. A general court-jurisdiction clause does not anticipate a statutory tribunal carve-out.
PDPA enforcement runs through the Commission, not through this contractual jurisdiction clause. The clause cannot and does not displace regulatory enforcement.

clauses.document_type: Internship Agreement (unsigned counterpart in corpus)
clauses.clause_text: client will pay you a fixed stipend of [BANDED: SGD 1,000-1,500] for the period of 4 weeks, paid directly to a nominated bank account in Singapore. The payment of your salary shall be subject to such statutory deductions and/or withholdings as may be required in accordance with applicable legislation in force from time to time. The client shall have the right to deduct from your salary any inadvertent overpayment of salary or other relevant payments under this Agreement. There shall be no entitlement to payment in respect of overtime.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: POTENTIAL CONTRADICTION. 'There shall be no entitlement to payment in respect of overtime' is an absolute contractual exclusion. The stipend is far below the $2,600 non-workman threshold in s 35, so if this is a contract of service, Part 4 applies and s 38(4) mandates overtime at not less than 1.5x. A contract cannot exclude a Part 4 entitlement by agreement. Contrast DOC-001 clause 6, which preserves 'overtime pay based on statutory rates, if applicable'. Two intern contracts, same statute, opposite drafting.
No payment date is stated at all — only that the stipend is 'for the period of 4 weeks'. The clause does not engage s 21's timing requirement one way or the other.
Recovery of overpayment is a permitted category, but the clause states no caps.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 95A read with reg 6(1) of the KET Regulations
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The engagement runs 7 July to 1 August — 26 days, comfortably over the 14-day threshold in reg 6(1). So written Key Employment Terms are required within 14 days of the start of employment. The KET list includes overtime terms, which this clause purports to exclude.
Same non-obvious dependency as DOC-001 clause 2(a) — name plus bank account number plus income is the reg 3 significant-harm combination.

clauses.document_type: Internship Agreement (unsigned counterpart in corpus)
clauses.clause_text: Your working hours shall be such hours as the client may from time to time deem appropriate and as may be necessary to achieve the purposes of the client and shall include the hours from 08:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. from Monday to Friday and, when necessary, after such hours without further remuneration.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: CONTRADICTED. 'after such hours without further remuneration' directly conflicts with s 38(4)'s 1.5x overtime rate for Part 4 employees, and the open-ended 'such hours as the client may deem appropriate' conflicts with the s 38(5) 72-hour monthly cap and the s 38(8) 12-hour daily cap.
No rest day is specified anywhere in the document. Contrast DOC-001 clause 6, which names Sunday.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests, in effect 1 Dec 2024
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: This document is dated 18 June 2025, six months after the guidelines took effect, and contains no FWA request pathway at all. DOC-001 at least gestures at FWAs. Existence and date verified; detailed requirements UNVERIFIED.

clauses.document_type: Internship Agreement (unsigned counterpart in corpus)
clauses.clause_text: In the event of absence or lateness for whatever reason including illness, you shall immediately notify the client by telephone, and a medical certificate from a doctor approved by the client or from a government hospital or clinic, or medical specialists to whom you are referred by a doctor approved by the client, certifying your physical condition, shall be delivered to the client.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The clause is headed SICK LEAVE but confers no sick leave entitlement whatsoever — it is purely a notification and medical-certificate duty. Separately, the engagement is 26 days, well under the 3-month qualifying period in s 89, so no statutory paid sick leave arises in any event. The heading promises an entitlement the clause does not deliver.
Compels delivery of medical certificates 'certifying your physical condition' to the employer. Health data in the reg 3 Schedule, combined with name, deems a breach to cause significant harm.
Requires an approved-doctor certificate but sets no limit on what the employer may do with it or how long it may be kept.

pdpa_impact.explanation: Compels collection of health data with no purpose limitation, no retention limit, and no handling protocol.

clauses.document_type: Internship Agreement (unsigned counterpart in corpus)
clauses.clause_text: All appointments are based on the information furnished in the course of applying for the post with [the client]. Hence, any false statement or information furnished during the course of application might lead to dismissal without notice. All internship are made subject to the approval of a training permit (if applicable) from the local immigration authorities.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Verification of application information is an evaluative purpose — no consent needed, no notification duty.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: Training Work Permit / Training Employment Pass
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: STALE TERMINOLOGY. The clause refers to 'a training permit (if applicable) from the local immigration authorities'. Work passes in Singapore are administered by MOM, not the immigration authority, and the current instruments are the Training Employment Pass and the Training Work Permit. The phrasing is loose enough to survive, but it points at the wrong regulator.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 26 (fair consideration, binds all employers regardless of size)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: On commencement, work-pass hiring will carry a statutory pre-application advertising and good-faith-consideration duty. This clause addresses only the permit outcome, not the employer's process.

clauses.document_type: Internship Agreement (unsigned counterpart in corpus)
clauses.clause_text: The terms and conditions as stipulated above shall be interpreted in accordance to the laws of the Republic of Singapore. In the event of any dispute, the parties shall submit to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Courts of the Republic of Singapore.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Same exposure as DOC-001 clause 21 — a general court-jurisdiction clause that does not anticipate the Employment Claims Tribunal carve-out for discrimination claims up to $250,000.

clauses.document_type: Internship Agreement (unsigned counterpart in corpus)
clauses.clause_text: The client collects, uses, discloses, retains and processes personal data concerning employees for the purpose of efficient human resource management. You agree to the client doing so and hereby give full consent to the client to furnish your relevant personal data to the appropriate and relevant parties in accordance with the principles of the client's policy on personal data protection. The client has established proper safeguards to prevent the misuse of such data and where the transfer of data outside Singapore is involved, appropriate measures are taken to ensure that adequate safeguards are in place. The client takes all reasonable steps to ensure that the data is accurate, complete, current and relevant. If you consider your data to be inaccurate or if you simply wish to have access to such data to verify it, you may do so by contacting the Human Resource Department. It is your responsibility to inform the client of any inaccuracies with respect to your personal data. It is also your legal duty to protect any person's personal data that may come into your possession during your internship with the client against any unauthorized access or processing. The client may, from time to time, monitor your use of client network resources (including e-mails, phone calls and the Internet) primarily for the following purposes: (i) facilitating the business of the client; (ii) maintaining a stable network environment for communications within the client, and communications with external parties; (iii) responding to any legal processes or to investigate any suspected breach of your obligations under this Agreement or the client's policies; and (iv) providing information to the client's management to ensure the proper utilization of the client's resources. A separate Annex, indicating the types of personal data, the purposes for the collection, use and/or processing of such data and the parties to which such personal data may be disclosed to, is attached.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Same architectural choice as DOC-001 clause 14 — 'hereby give full consent' — with the same s 16 revocability weakness.
'Efficient human resource management' is squarely within managing the employment relationship. Consent was not required.

BETTER THAN DOC-001 ON THIS POINT. The clause states the purpose in-line ('efficient human resource management'), lists the network-monitoring purposes exhaustively, and refers to an attached Annex specifying data types, purposes and recipients. That attached-Annex structure is much closer to what s 20(4) actually requires than DOC-001's reference to an unattached, unilaterally-mutable external Group notice.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: para 6.21 (IT resource monitoring is a listed management purpose)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The network-monitoring limb aligns with PDPC's non-exhaustive list of employment-management purposes.

WEAKER THAN DOC-001 ON THIS POINT. 'Appropriate measures are taken to ensure that adequate safeguards are in place' does not even use the statutory 'comparable standard of protection' formulation, names no destination countries, and identifies no legal mechanism.

'Adequate safeguards' is not one of the four routes to legally enforceable obligations. Capgemini is a multinational group with 'Related Bodies Corporate' defined in clause 1 — the binding-corporate-rules route in reg 11 is available to it and is not invoked.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: reg 12 as amended, in force 2 March 2026
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: This document is dated 18 June 2025 — NINE MONTHS BEFORE the certification expansion. It could not have anticipated it. This is the cleanest example in the corpus of a document that was reasonable when drafted and has since been overtaken.

Routes queries to 'the Human Resource Department' rather than to a designated individual. s 11(3) requires designating one or more INDIVIDUALS, and s 11(5) requires publishing the business contact information of at least one. A department is not an individual.
The clause provides an access-and-correction pathway, which is a genuine strength — it maps to the Access and Correction Obligations rather than ignoring them.

'It is also your legal duty to protect any person's personal data that may come into your possession' is the closest any document in this corpus comes to acknowledging the intern's own PDPA exposure. It correctly frames it as a LEGAL duty rather than a contractual one. But it names no statute, describes no offence, and creates no reporting route.
Silent on breach notification, as with every other document in the corpus.

pdpa_impact.explanation: Better than DOC-001 on notification (in-line purposes plus an attached Annex) and on access/correction; WORSE on cross-border transfer ('adequate safeguards' does not even track the statutory wording) and on the DPO (a department, not a designated individual). Same stale consent architecture. Same total silence on breach notification. The fact that it is better in some respects and worse in others than a document from the same corpus is exactly why a change-impact tool cannot treat 'has a PDPA clause' as a binary.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter, small Singapore law firm
clauses.clause_heading: ALLOWANCE & BENEFITS — exclusion of employee benefits
clauses.clause_text: For the avoidance of doubt, as an intern, you will not receive any employee benefits that regular employees receive, including but not limited to health insurance, vacation, or sick pay.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: CONTRADICTED, IF THE ENGAGEMENT IS A CONTRACT OF SERVICE. The clause purports to exclude annual leave and sick pay by labelling the individual 'an intern'. MOM is explicit that the label does not decide the question — coverage turns on whether there is a contract of service. The document itself supplies control indicators: fixed hours (cl 3.1), a supervisor, absence-notification duties (cl 3.2), exclusivity (cl 4.3), disciplinary consequences (cl 4.8). In practice s 88A and s 89 both require 3 months' service and this engagement is 26 days, so the entitlements would not arise on these facts — but the clause states a general legal proposition that is wrong as drafted.
regulatory_dependencies.confidence: medium — the statutory test is verified; the outcome is a factual determination

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: MOST SERIOUS SINGLE EXPOSURE IN THE CORPUS. The clause affirmatively states the intern gets no health insurance. WIC insurance is mandatory for employees on a contract of service doing non-manual work earning under $2,600/month, and failing to insure is an offence carrying up to $10,000 and 12 months. WIC insurance is not an 'employee benefit' the parties can contract out of — it is a statutory duty on the employer.
No CPF clause anywhere in the document. The student-endorsement exemption is conditional on holding institutional approval documentation; nothing here records that it was obtained.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter, small Singapore law firm
clauses.clause_text: It is your responsibility to inform the Firm and your supervisor in a timely manner if you are unable to attend work for any reason. You must provide notice to your supervisor or the Firm at least 24 hours in advance of any anticipated absence, or as soon as possible in case of unexpected illness or emergency.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: The document requires absence notification but nowhere requires or mentions a medical certificate. Contrast DOC-001 cl 8 and DOC-002 cl 7, both of which do. On these facts the 3-month qualifying period is not met, so no statutory sick leave arises.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter, small Singapore law firm
clauses.clause_heading: CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE — Compliance with Laws and Regulations
clauses.clause_text: You must comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including but not limited to those related to data protection, privacy, and intellectual property.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: THE PUREST EXAMPLE OF 'INSUFFICIENT' IN THE CORPUS. This is the document's ONLY data protection provision — a single sentence, in a conduct clause, telling the intern to obey the law. It is not wrong. It is also completely non-operative: it names no statute, states no obligation, creates no process, and gives the intern nothing to actually do. An intern at a law firm handles clients' personal data and faces personal criminal liability under ss 48D-48E for mishandling it. This sentence does not tell her that.

regulatory_dependencies.provision: s 12 (Accountability — written policies, complaints process, communicate to staff)
regulatory_dependencies.relationship: A generic 'comply with the law' instruction is not the communication of written policies and practices that s 12(c) requires.

The document contains NO notification of the purposes for which the firm collects and uses the intern's own personal data. Compliance-with-law language addresses the intern's duties to others; it does not discharge the firm's own duty to her.
No DPO named and no contact route given.

pdpa_impact.explanation: Says something true — comply with data protection law — but discharges none of the firm's own PDPA obligations and gives the intern no operative guidance. Compare with DOC-001 cl 14 and DOC-002 cl 15, which at least attempt purposes, transfer and access. Three documents, three completely different depths of PDPA treatment, all in the same corpus, all governing the same person.

clauses.document_type: Internship offer letter, small Singapore law firm
clauses.clause_text: During the course of your internship with the Firm, you may have access to and become acquainted with various trade secrets, confidential information and operations, business strategies, customer lists, dealings or any information concerning the organization, business, finance, transactions or affairs of the Firm and other intellectual property (collectively, "Confidential Information") belonging to the Firm and its clients. You agree to maintain the confidentiality of all Confidential Information and not to disclose any Confidential Information to any third party or use it for any purpose other than in the performance of your internship duties with the Firm.

regulatory_dependencies.relationship: Expressly extends to information belonging to the Firm's CLIENTS. At a law firm this means third parties' personal data, often sensitive. The intern's exposure under ss 48D-48E is at its highest here, and the clause frames the duty as owed to the Firm alone.

demo_scenario_primary.title: The intern who is a data subject, a data handler, and a criminal liability — all at once
demo_scenario_primary.status: REAL AND IN FORCE. Not hypothetical. Not invented.
demo_scenario_primary.why_this_scenario: It is real, it is Singapore-specific, the most recent piece landed six months before the pitch, it hits all five documents differently, and — critically — it produces all four impact types rather than a uniform find-and-replace. It also has a live enforcement record, so the harm is not speculative.

the_change.summary: PDPA obligations have moved in three separable waves, and the corpus straddles all three.

wave_1.what: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2020 (Act 40 of 2020). Restructured the consent architecture — new First Schedule with the Legitimate Interests Part, including the employment-management exception at Part 3 para 10 and the evaluative-purposes exception at Part 3 para 2. Added mandatory breach notification at Part 6A (ss 26A-26E). Added individual criminal offences at Part 9B (ss 48C-48F).
wave_1.in_force: 1 February 2021 for the bulk; 1 October 2022 for the turnover-based penalty in s 24 (10% of annual Singapore turnover where that exceeds $10 million).

wave_2.what: PDPC Advisory Guidelines on the PDPA for Selected Topics, Chapter 6 (Employment), REVISED. Confirms expressly that employment-relationship handling does not require consent, that notification of purposes is what is owed instead, and that the employment contract is an accepted vehicle for that notification.
wave_2.in_force: Revised 23 May 2024. Soft law, but it is the regulator telling the market that consent-based HR clauses are solving the wrong problem.

wave_3.what: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (S 86/2026). Expanded the certifications recognised under reg 12 for cross-border transfer beyond APEC CBPR/PRP to include the Global CBPR System and the Global Privacy Recognition for Processors System.
wave_3.in_force: 2 MARCH 2026 — six months before this pitch. Made 26 February 2026.
wave_3.why_it_matters_for_the_demo: This is the freshest real change available. DOC-002 (June 2025) predates it by nine months and could not have anticipated it. DOC-001 (April 2026) postdates it by six weeks and still does not reflect it. That contrast — one document excusably stale, one inexcusably stale, same change — is the demo's sharpest single moment.

dormant.what: Part 6B (ss 26F-26J) and the Twelfth Schedule — the Data Portability Obligation. Enacted by the 2020 Amendment Act.
dormant.status: STILL NOT COMMENCED as at 5 September 2026. Verified by the absence of Part 6B and of a Twelfth Schedule from the current consolidated Act's table of contents.
dormant.why_it_matters_for_the_demo: This is the resilience argument in one fact. A provision has been sitting on the statute book, gazetted and drafted, for nearly six years without commencing. A tool that is merely RESPONSIVE learns about it on commencement day. A tool that is RESILIENT already knows which clauses in which documents will need a portability request pathway, and can stage the amendment before the Minister signs the notification. Do not overclaim: there is no announced commencement date, and I found no PDPC statement on whether or when it will commence.

impact_map.impact_type: INSUFFICIENT (primary), plus STALE and NEWLY REQUIRED
impact_map.how: Cross-border transfer promises 'reasonable steps to ensure ... comparable protection'. reg 11 of the PDP Regulations 2021 requires legally enforceable obligations by one of four routes — law, a contract specifying destination countries, binding corporate rules, or another binding instrument. 'Reasonable steps' is none of them, and no destination countries are named. Separately STALE: built on consent when the employment-management exception has been available since 2021 and PDPC said in May 2024 that consent is not required — the employer has chosen a basis the intern can revoke under s 16 over one she cannot. Separately NEWLY REQUIRED: no breach-notification pathway, and no reference to the certification route expanded on 2 March 2026, six weeks before signature.
impact_map.propagation: Rewrite the transfer limb onto binding corporate rules or an intra-group contract naming destination countries; re-base the clause from consent onto First Schedule Part 3 para 10 plus an s 20(4) notification; add a breach-escalation route.

impact_map.impact_type: INSUFFICIENT (primary), plus STALE and NEWLY REQUIRED
impact_map.how: Hit by the SAME change but in a DIFFERENT PLACE. Stronger than DOC-001 on notification — it states purposes in-line, enumerates the network-monitoring purposes, and attaches an Annex of data types, purposes and recipients, which is close to what s 20(4) actually wants. Stronger on access and correction. But WEAKER on transfer: 'adequate safeguards' does not even track the statutory 'comparable standard' wording, let alone reg 11's four routes. And weaker on the DPO: it routes queries to 'the Human Resource Department', where s 11(3) requires designating one or more INDIVIDUALS and s 11(5) requires publishing at least one individual's business contact information.
impact_map.propagation: Different remedy from DOC-001: the notification limb is fine and should be left alone; the transfer limb and the DPO designation both need replacing. A tool that proposed the same edit to both documents would be wrong.

impact_map.document: Silverbirch (small law firm) — clause 4.5, Compliance with Laws and Regulations
impact_map.how: The document's entire data protection content is one sentence in a conduct clause telling the intern to comply with data protection law. Nothing is contradicted, because nothing is asserted. There is no notification of purposes to the intern, no DPO, no transfer position, no retention position, no breach route. And the intern is at a LAW FIRM handling client personal data (cl 7.1 expressly extends confidentiality to information belonging to the Firm's clients), so her personal exposure under ss 48D-48E is at its highest of anyone in the corpus, and the document tells her nothing about it. Clause 7.3 compounds it by sunsetting the confidentiality obligation after one year, inviting the inference that her duties regarding client personal data also expire. They do not.
impact_map.propagation: Nothing to amend. A data protection clause must be ADDED, from scratch, along with a client-data handling protocol and a breach-escalation route.

impact_map.document: Anson Chambers (small law firm) — the face of the letter
impact_map.how: A four-paragraph letter that collects the individual's full name, an alternative name, her NRIC/FIN number and her full residential address, and pays her an allowance — and contains no data protection provision of any kind. Under reg 3 of the Breach Notification Regulations, name-or-identification-number combined with income data is precisely the significant-harm combination. The document performs a regulated act and carries no regulatory content whatsoever.
impact_map.propagation: The gap is total. This document cannot be patched clause by clause; it needs to be replaced with one that meets s 95A KET requirements and carries an s 20(4) notification.

impact_map.document: The drafting-exercise Master Agreement — clause 15, Confidentiality
impact_map.impact_type: NEWLY REQUIRED, in a TEMPLATE rather than an executed contract
impact_map.how: Clauses 5 and 6 run a Tenant Candidate Evaluation Table scoring identified individuals on Team Quality and Cultural Fit with an Interview Assessment section, and allocate that process between two contracting parties plus a Property Manager. That is a multi-party personal-data processing architecture. The agreement has a commercial confidentiality clause protecting the PARTIES and no data protection clause protecting the DATA SUBJECTS. Confidentiality between the parties does nothing for the individuals being scored.
impact_map.propagation: This is the highest-leverage fix in the corpus because the document is a precedent, not a one-off. Every future agreement drafted from it inherits the gap. Fixing the template fixes every unwritten future document; fixing a signed contract fixes one.

impact_map.document: Confidentiality clauses in EssilorLuxottica (cl 10) and Silverbirch (cl 7.1)
impact_map.impact_type: INSUFFICIENT — the operational gap, and the best single point in the pitch
impact_map.how: s 26D(1) gives the organisation 3 CALENDAR DAYS from its assessment to notify PDPC. The s 26C duty to assess is triggered by credible grounds to believe a breach occurred — and credible grounds usually arrive because a member of staff escalates something. Both clauses impose comprehensive confidentiality duties and create NO internal reporting or escalation route. An intern who notices a breach is contractually instructed to keep quiet, not to report. The employer's compliance with a statutory deadline therefore depends on a reporting path its own contract does not create, and mildly discourages.
impact_map.propagation: Add a breach-escalation duty to every confidentiality clause in the corpus. This is a single edit pattern that propagates across four of the five documents — exactly the kind of finding the problem statement asks for.

coverage_asymmetry.headline: The same change lands on these five documents through three different coverage doors. This is what makes the scenario worth demonstrating rather than merely describing.
points: PDPA coverage does NOT depend on a contract of service. s 2(1) defines 'employee' to include a volunteer and 'employment' to include unpaid volunteer work. So PDPA reaches further than the Employment Act does — an unpaid intern who falls outside the EA is very likely still inside the PDPA. Flag honestly: PDPC has issued no guidance on interns and the word does not appear in the 62-page Selected Topics guidelines. This is an inference from the statutory text.

The two multinationals (DOC-001, DOC-002) both transfer intern data across borders to group affiliates, so s 26 and reg 11 bite hard on both — and both fail it, but by different wording and with different available fixes (DOC-002 defines 'Related Bodies Corporate' in clause 1, so the binding-corporate-rules route in reg 11 is squarely available to it and is not invoked).

The two small law firms (DOC-003, DOC-004) have no cross-border exposure at all, so s 26 is irrelevant to them. Their exposure is entirely on the other side: they hold CLIENT personal data and put interns in contact with it, with no handling protocol. Same statute, opposite pressure point.

The turnover-based penalty at s 48J(3) — 10% of annual Singapore turnover above $10 million, otherwise capped at $1 million — scales with the organisation. The identical breach produces a materially different penalty exposure for EssilorLuxottica than for a small firm. The regulation is uniform; the risk is not.

DOC-005 is not an employment document at all, so the employment-management exception is unavailable to it. Its personal-data flows concern third-party tenant candidates, who would need an ordinary consent or another exception. A tool that classified the corpus as 'employment contracts' and applied an employment lens uniformly would get this document exactly wrong.

demo_scenarios_secondary.title: Workplace Fairness Act 2025 commencement
demo_scenarios_secondary.status: REAL, PASSED, NOT YET IN FORCE. Act 8 of 2025, passed 8 Jan 2025, assented 3 Feb 2025. SSO shows 'Uncommenced' as at 5 Sep 2026. MOM's stated target is end-2027. The companion Workplace Fairness (Dispute Resolution) Act 2025 (Act 22 of 2025) is also uncommenced.

But it is NOT YET IN FORCE, and a pitch whose centrepiece is an uncommenced Act invites the obvious question from the bench. Use it as the second act, framed honestly as a change you can prepare for precisely BECAUSE it has not commenced.
what_it_hits: s 27 grievance handling — mandatory written process, employees informed in writing, written records kept. NO document in the corpus has any grievance process at all. Pure NEWLY REQUIRED across DOC-001 and DOC-002.

s 19 discriminatory job advertisements and s 26 fair consideration — s 26 binds ALL employers regardless of size, so it reaches DOC-003 and DOC-004 too, and both are silent. DOC-001 cl 1(a) and DOC-002 cl 11 address only the candidate's pass, never the employer's pre-application advertising duty.

s 8(k) mental health condition as a protected characteristic — interacts directly with DOC-001 cl 8, which routes every medical certificate to the employer with disciplinary consequences for non-production.

DOC-003 and DOC-004: almost certainly under the 25-employee threshold, so exempt from everything except s 26, and left governed by the TGFEP — which is NOT superseded and continues to run alongside. demo_scenarios_secondary.title: Data portability commencement — the dormant provision
demo_scenarios_secondary.status: ENACTED BUT NOT COMMENCED. Part 6B (ss 26F-26J) and the Twelfth Schedule were inserted by the 2020 Amendment Act and have still not come into force as at 5 September 2026, verified by their absence from the current consolidated Act's table of contents. There is NO announced commencement date and I found no PDPC statement on whether or when it will commence.
demo_scenarios_secondary.why_ranked_fourth_but_worth_the_closing_: It has the least immediate impact and the best rhetoric. A provision drafted, passed and gazetted nearly six years ago is still sitting there. Awareness is not the gap — everybody knows it exists. The gap is that nobody has mapped which clauses in which documents will need to change on the day it commences. That is precisely the problem statement's distinction between being responsive and being resilient, and this is the cleanest real example of it in Singapore law.
demo_scenarios_secondary.honesty_warning: Do NOT state or imply a commencement date. There isn't one. The strength of this example is that it has been pending indefinitely, not that it is imminent.
